A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PH-VAE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched across pagination and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real-world experiments, multivariate dependence measurements, hyperparameter ablations, and training-time measurements in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds evaluated decoder baselines in Table 1 and quantitative real-world tail-risk results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The shared Gaussian latent variable, acyclic PH decoder, parameter constraints, ELBO, uniformization procedure, and sampling algorithms are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices C–D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four synthetic univariate distributions, Danish Fire Insurance losses, word-frequency data, synthetic multivariate data, and five-equity financial returns. The additional results introduce no new dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LogNormal-VAE and Gamma-VAE across all four synthetic distributions, substantially broadening the central decoder-family comparison beyond Gaussian VAE, t-VAE, and xVAE. Comparator membership in the real-world and multivariate comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New Table 2 adds real-world quantile and CVaR error evaluation at q = 0.95, 0.99, and 0.995, supplementing the existing CCDF diagnostics. The Pareto ablation column changes from Tail CoExErr@99 to Q99 error while retaining identical numbers; this revises the reported metric without establishing that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The phase-count and KL-weight sweeps, shared-latent comparisons, independence controls, PH approximation illustrations, and runtime analysis retain the same configurations and numerical evidence. Apart from the ablation metric relabeling, no revised analysis or new robustness experiment is documented; the added limitations are discussion.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 retains multiple independent training runs and mean plus one standard deviation, without specifying a run count. Appendix B.4 also retains its seed-averaging statement. Added result entries use the existing uncertainty-reporting format; no new statistical procedure or explicit increase in runs is reported.

E6.justification: The added Table 1 comparisons change the reported ranking on Burr Q99 error: Gamma-VAE scores 0.166 and LogNormal-VAE 0.379, below PH-VAE's retained 0.599. New Table 2 provides quantitative tail-risk evidence for both real-world univariate datasets, previously assessed through plots; for example, Danish Fire CVaR error at q = 0.99 is 0.200 for PH-VAE versus 0.809 for Gaussian VAE. Previously reported numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, PH representation theorem, universality discussion, asymptotic analysis, and likelihood derivations are unchanged. The new finite-range qualifications restate the scope already discussed in Section 2.3 and Appendix C rather than adding or correcting formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract changes recovery of heavy-tailed distributions to approximation and explicitly qualifies tail modeling as finite-range and observed. The conclusion similarly adds observed. These refine the headline claims while retaining the same method, novelty claim, and principal contributions.

C2.justification: A new Limitations paragraph discusses insufficient or truncated extreme observations, instability with little data, and limited latent capacity in high dimensions. Its asymptotic light-tail qualification was already present elsewhere in v1. Table 1's caption also narrows the performance interpretation to nearly all datasets and metrics.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same parameterization details, log-variance bounds, uniformization tolerance, optimization description, and runtime information. No implementation or access details are added for the new baselines, and the new CVaR evaluation receives no dedicated estimation description.

R1.justification: Appendix C.6 replaces the Feldmann et al. (1998) internet-traffic reference with Feldmann and Whitt (1998), whose listed work concerns exponential-mixture approximation of long-tail distributions. The remaining related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract and conclusion edits, adds a Limitations paragraph and Acknowledgements section, and adds publication information. The main narrative, section organization, and appendix exposition otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows and revised caption and best-value emphasis; a new real-world results table is inserted; and the ablation metric header is corrected. Existing figures are retained, with local float relocation, table renumbering, and text reflow rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The additional decoder comparisons and quantitative real-world tail-risk results strengthen the empirical assessment, while the finite-range wording and explicit limitations better qualify applicability. The gains are limited by incomplete integration: Section 4.1 still claims PH-VAE wins every case despite the new Burr results favoring Gamma-VAE and LogNormal-VAE, and the added baselines and CVaR evaluation lack dedicated implementation details.
